facts.statement: The genus Quasianosteosaurus was first named by Maisch and Matzke in 2003.
facts.quote: It was first named by Michael Werner Maisch and Andreas Theodor Matzke in 2003

facts.statement: The species is known only from a single partial skull fossil, MNHN Nr. SVT 331, which preserves the snout and eye regions.
facts.quote: Quasianosteosaurus is known only from the holotype MNHN Nr. SVT 331, a partial three-dimensionally preserved skull consisting of the snout and orbital and postorbital regions.

facts.statement: Its skull is the largest known Early Triassic ichthyosaur skull, measuring an estimated 50 cm in length.
facts.quote: The skull is by far the largest Early Triassic ichthyosaur skull known, with an estimated cranial length of 50 cm.

facts.statement: This basal ichthyosaur lived during the late Early Triassic in Spitsbergen, part of the Svalbard archipelago in Norway.
facts.quote: Quasianosteosaurus is an extinct genus of basal ichthyosaur known from the late Early Triassic (late Olenekian stage) of Spitsbergen of the Svalbard archipelago, Norway.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis classifies Quasianosteosaurus as a basal ichthyosaur that is the sister taxon to Hueneosauria.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis performed by Maisch & Matzke (2003) found it to be a basal ichthyosaur, sister taxon to Hueneosauria.

facts.statement: The genus belongs to the family Quasianosteosauridae.
The fossil was collected from the Sticky Keep Formation at Mount Viking in the Sassendalen area.
facts.quote: It was collected from the lowermost Grippia Niveau of the Sticky Keep Formation (Spathian substage), Sassendalen Group at Mount Viking, Sassendalen.

rejected.statement: The name Quasianosteosaurus means "almost boneless lizard" because the holotype is mostly a natural cast of the skull with very little original bone.
rejected.quote: The generic name is derived from Latin quasi, "almost", and Greek anosteos, "boneless" and sauros, "lizard", regarding the preservation of the holotype which is almost exclusively a natural cast of the skull with very little original bone.
